newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares were knocked by expectations of a weaker Wall Street opening on Tuesday while gold counters ended only slightly firmer amid thin volumes.
The market started positive after Wall Street gained 143 points to a new record high on Monday night. But futures players combined with weaker S&P futures hit the industrial index.

"The market was very, very choppy. It opened up on the Dow's (overnight) gains but pulled back later. When the Dow looked like it would open weaker the market initially eased but then came back again as Wall Street turned positive," a dealer said.
He said expectations of a weak Wall Street opening on Tuesday hit local industrial shares shortly before the close but they recovered to end flat as Wall Street turned positive.
Volumes traded were worth over 900 million rand, with most blue chips enjoying some interest.

Gold shares ended slightly firmer after bullion gained three dollars on Monday. But dealers said volumes were thin and players were concerned that the rise in the bullion price could not be sustained.
"Golds were largely firmer on the back of thin volumes. The market is concerned whether the firmness in gold price will continue," Dominic Rey, international trader at Investec told Reuters.
He added that the gold price was helped in part by the Bre-X Minerals Ltd debacle.
The market was seen taking its cue from Wall Street on Wednesday.
The all-share index ended 21.6 points stronger at 7,212.0 points, the industrial index was up 5.3 points to 8,568.7 points and the gold index added 6.6 points to 1,212.3 points.
Edgars shares fell 475 cents to 110 rand after it reported year results below analysts' expectations.
Big volumes were seen in a wide spectrum of shares with SAB rising 25 cents to 133 rand in volume worth nearly 60 million rand. Hoechst lost five cents to 345 cents also in large volume.
PPC shares were down 50 cents to 69 rand after posting poor results, confounding analysts who had expected a modest rise in earnings.
Altech jumped 700 cents, or 9.33 percent, to 82 rand on the back of healthy year results published on Monday.
Shares in JCI, recently taken over by black empowerment consortium African Mining Group, were pressured in the morning after the resignation of managing director, Bill Nairn.
Shares recovered some early losses ending down 35 cents to 42.50 rand in what dealers said was likely to be a shortlived pressure on the share.

JCI's new chairman, Mzi Khumalo, said on Tuesday that with his increasing involvement in the business of the company, it had become clear that there was little reason to maintain both the position of executive chairman and managing director.

JCI's holding company Saflife was strained losing 75 cents to 20.15 rand after it opened higher at 21.30 rand. Massive volumes have recently been seen in the group's nil paid letters which traded over 20 million shares on Tuesday.
Near-dated industrial share futures were flat after climbing in the morning on Wall Street's overnight gains.
Gold contracts were firmer on a better bullion price with moderate volumes traded as players possibly hedged in the market, dealers said.
The June all-share contract was last at 6,695/711 from 6,695, the industrial contract was at 8,416/25 from 8,422 and the gold contract was at 859/62 from 852.
-- Charles Phahlane, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
